data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name Nathan, which means 'given by God'. Nathias appears in the Old Testament as the name of a Levite musician and priest. It's also the name of a companion of St. Paul mentioned in the New Testament. The name Nathias carries the meaning “Given by God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Nathias usually hope their child will grow to embody given by god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the gift of God's presence and guidance.
data.etymology: Nathias belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Given by God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nathias total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_greek.name: Νάθιας
in_greek.long_meaning: Νάθιας είναι όνομα το οποίο αποτελείται από τις λέξεις νάθ, δώρον, και ιας, δύναμη, και σημαίνει δώρον Θεού με δύναμη, το όνομα αυτό χρησιμοποιήθηκε στην πρώιμη εκκλησία και έχει σπουδαία σημασία στην χριστιανική παράδοση

in_latin.name: Nathias

In addition, the name's appearance in the New Testament as a companion of St. Paul reflects the influence and spread of Christianity throughout history.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Nathias carries a deep spiritual significance, as it is derived from the Hebrew name Nathan, which means 'given by God'. This name affirms the belief that every person is a unique creation of God, and it serves as a reminder of the importance of trusting in God's guidance and protection. It also reflects the spiritual roles of music and religious service in connecting individuals to the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nathias may symbolize a fighter for divine wisdom and truth, derived from the Hebrew origin meaning "who gives". The name may spiritually represent a warrior of faith, dedicated to seeking and sharing God's guidance in life.

historical_references.reference: The name Nathias is mentioned in the New Testament in Acts 2:3, describing a man named Joseph, also known as Bar-Jesus, or Justus, who was a Levite and a native of Cyprus. He and his wife Tabitha (Dorcas) were well known for their acts of kindness and generosity. She died and was brought back to life by Peter.

Nathanael is a name given to a figure in the New Testament, mentioned in the Gospel of John. He was a man from Bethsaida in Galilee and was described by Philip as an Israelite without guile. Jesus praised Nathanael for his faith, prophesying that he would see heaven before he died.
